overviewHtml:
This ungraded knowledge check assesses your understanding of Husserl's analysis of time-consciousness. You'll be asked about primal impression, retention, protention, the difference between retention and recollection, and the melody example.

Note: Use this to test yourself, review the feedback on any questions you miss, and retry until you feel confident before moving forward.

forms.stemHtml: As you hear the third note of a melody, how is the second note given?

options.html: It's recalled by a new act of remembering
options.text: It's recalled by a new act of remembering
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Recalling is a new act that re-presents the past. The second note is retained: still given in the present experience, as just past.

options.html: It's retained, still given as just past
options.text: It's retained, still given as just past
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The second note is held in retention. It's part of your present hearing, given as just past, not recalled by a separate act.

options.html: It's no longer given in experience at all
options.text: It's no longer given in experience at all
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. If the second note were gone, you'd hear only isolated tones. It's retained, still given as just past.

options.html: It's anticipated as the note about to come
options.text: It's anticipated as the note about to come
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Anticipating what's about to come is protention. The second note is retained, still given as just past.

options.html: Retention lasts a few seconds, recollection much longer
options.text: Retention lasts a few seconds, recollection much longer
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The difference is structural, not only a matter of duration. Retention is part of the present experience, and recollection is a new act that re-presents the past.

options.html: Retention is part of present experience; recollection is a new act
options.text: Retention is part of present experience; recollection is a new act
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Retention belongs to the present perception and gives the just-past as itself. Recollection is a separate act that re-presents a past experience after a gap.

options.html: Retention is voluntary, and recollection happens automatically
options.text: Retention is voluntary, and recollection happens automatically
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. It's closer to the reverse. Retention happens with every perception. The key difference is that retention is part of present experience, while recollection is a new act.

options.html: Retention concerns sounds, and recollection concerns images
options.text: Retention concerns sounds, and recollection concerns images
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Both can concern any kind of object. Retention is part of present experience, while recollection is a new act that re-presents the past.

forms.stemHtml: Which of the following are phases of a single present experience, on Husserl's account? (Select all that apply.)

options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Primal impression is the now-phase.
Correct! Retention holds the just-past in the present experience.
Correct! Protention is the open anticipation of what is about to come.
Sorry, that's incorrect. Recollection isn't a phase of the present experience. It's a separate act that re-presents the past.
Sorry, that's incorrect. Protention isn't a deliberate prediction. It's an open anticipation built into experience. Prediction isn't one of Husserl's phases.

forms.stemHtml: Walking down stairs in the dark, you expect one more step and your foot meets nothing. What is Husserl's term for the anticipation this surprise reveals? Enter one word.

options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The jolt shows that your experience already contained an anticipation of the next step, which the world failed to fulfill.
Sorry, that's incorrect. Retention holds the just-past. The anticipation of what is about to come is protention.

forms.defaultFeedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The anticipation of what is about to come, revealed here by surprise, is protention.

forms.stemHtml: Husserl compares the retained phases of experience to a comet's tail. What does the image convey?

options.html: Each now is followed by a sudden break in experience
options.text: Each now is followed by a sudden break in experience
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The image conveys continuity. Each now drags behind it a continuously fading tail of retained phases.

options.html: Past experiences return in bright flashes of memory
options.text: Past experiences return in bright flashes of memory
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. That describes recollection, not retention. The comet's tail conveys a continuously fading tail of retained phases behind each now.

options.html: Each now trails a fading tail of retained phases behind it
options.text: Each now trails a fading tail of retained phases behind it
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! As each new phase arrives, the previous ones sink back, still given but further past. That tail is what lets you hear a phrase.

options.html: Anticipation stretches far ahead of each present moment
options.text: Anticipation stretches far ahead of each present moment
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Anticipation is protention. The comet's tail conveys the fading tail of retained phases behind each now.

title: Time-Consciousness
